fields.title-post: Franchisor and franchisee: how to develop a good relationship?
fields.rt-blog-html:
Want to maximize the potential of your franchise network? The first and most important step is to establish a solid relationship between franchisor and franchisee. To achieve this, it's vital to foster communication, total transparency and ongoing support to ensure the success of your collaboration. As a franchisor, your role is not just to provide a concept, but also to accompany your franchisee every step of the way, from training to day-to-day management. Discover our practical tips for building a lasting relationship between franchisor and franchisee.

‍

Clearly defined roles and responsibilities

Franchisor and franchisee, the two key players in the franchise model, play distinct but complementary roles. Their relationship is based on a contractual partnership, with specific rights and obligations.

  • The franchisor: The franchisor owns the brand, the business model, and the know-how, which it passes on to the franchisee. Its primary role is to ensure the network’s long-term viability by maintaining consistent quality standards and supporting its franchisees.
  • The franchisee: An entrepreneur who operates the franchisor’s business model in exchange for an initial fee and royalties. The franchisee follows the franchisor’s processes and methods to ensure the success of their local outlet.

The franchisor's obligations :

  • Providing know-how,
  • Ongoing training,
  • Support the franchisee's development,
  • Ensure network consistency.

The franchisee's obligations :

  • Respect franchise standards,
  • Apply the know-how you've learned,
  • Pay royalties to the franchisor,
  • Participate in network development initiatives.

Their common expectations: According to the Fédération Française de la Franchise, in the document Qualité de la relation franchise et performance (2021), the relationship between franchisor and franchisee is based on a legally defined contractual framework, supported by regular communication and exchanges based on trust, all of which are essential to ensure the network's performance and longevity.

‍

Why is it essential to have a good franchisor-franchisee relationship?

The quality of the franchisor-franchisee relationship is crucial to the network’s longevity and success. According to the 14th edition of the Banque Populaire annual franchise survey, conducted in partnership with the French Franchise Federation (FFF), 64% of franchisors state that the relationship between franchisors and franchisees is an essential factor in the network’s successful development. 

A solid relationship between franchisors and franchisees guarantees several advantages:

  • Better store performance: A franchisee who receives proper guidance, training, and support is better able to implement the franchisor’s methods and standards, which leads to increased revenue.
  • Increased customer satisfaction: A consistent and seamless customer experience across all points of sale builds consumer trust and loyalty.
  • Stability and development of the network: by maintaining a good relationship, the franchisor limits departures and creates an atmosphere of collaboration and solidarity within the network.

👉 To find out more: How to effectively develop your fast-food franchise network

‍

How to communicate effectively?

Transparency and regular exchanges

Transparency and communication are essential right from the start. It's essential for both parties to communicate clearly and regularly, right from the initial discussions before signing the contract. As a franchisor, providing precise answers to the future franchisee's questions, and maintaining this transparency throughout the contract , contributes to a relationship of trust.

The franchisee, for their part, must commit to faithfully implementing the concept, while retaining the flexibility to make adjustments as needed. This coordination ensures a successful partnership, strengthening the network and the franchise’s success.

Continuing Education

The franchisor is required to train the franchisee to ensure compliance with brand standards. This training is essential to ensuring the smooth operation of the business. According to the annual survey by the Banque Populaire franchise, nearly 80% of franchisees report having received support for about ten days when they opened their retail location, which they consider to have been indispensable in helping them avoid initial mistakes and build their skills. 

Going forward, it is a good idea to offer regular refresher courses and additional training to keep pace with market changes or new products.

‍

Focus on the key role of network coordinators

Network coordinators play a key role in supporting franchisees. They serve as the link between headquarters and the retail locations. According to the survey, 73% of franchisees consider their role essential to the smooth functioning of the relationship with the franchisor. Through their regular visits, they provide advice, report challenges, and share best practices observed elsewhere in the network.

👉 Learn more: The role of a franchise network coordinator in the restaurant industry

‍

Digital tools to enhance the franchisor-franchisee relationship

Digital solutions are essential tools for strengthening the relationship between franchisors and franchisees. Thanks to tools such as performance tracking systems integrated into point-of-sale software, franchisees benefitfrom simplified day-to-day management.

For their part, franchisors can access figures and data from the various outlets in real time. Abdullah, NBK Franchise Development Director, explains: " I can create my menu and duplicate it easily in all my outlets. And in an instant, all the restaurants can have it on their till, on their kiosk, on their Click & Collect. "

👉 Read Abdullah's testimonial

‍

For a franchise to operate successfully and grow sustainably, the quality of the franchisor-franchisee relationship is essential. A good working relationship, transparent communication, and the right tools help optimize this relationship.
